source.title: Self-Augmentation: Generalizing Deep Networks to Unseen Classes for Few-Shot Learning
source.authors: Jinhwan Seo; Hong G Jung; Seong-Whan Lee

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports few-shot classification on classes disjoint from training classes, a different generalization target from the claim's held-out examples from the same distribution. It discusses memorization and cites related work, but does not test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The reported experiments evaluate classification of unseen classes using a few labeled examples. Those results concern few-shot generalization to disjoint classes, so they do not test the claim versions about same-distribution test error or its gap from training error.
record.test_reason: The study discusses memorization and generalization but tests none of V1–V8. Its experiments compare input augmentation, self-distillation and task-specific fine-tuning for classification of unseen classes. Regional dropout here replaces image patches; it does not test the network dropout intervention in V6. No random-label, width, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, magnitude-aware sharpness or memorized-example-removal comparison is reported.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that self-mix combined with self-distillation improves few-shot classification of unseen classes, and LRL further improves their method across the tested benchmarks, especially cross-domain 5-shot classification. Their attribution to alleviating memorization is an interpretation; they do not directly measure memorization.
record.recipe_differences: Few-shot learning method combining self-mix, self-distillation, and task-level fine-tuning; it does not reproduce the same-distribution train-test generalization experiments in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, shot count, regional dropout and self-distillation combination, number of classifiers, label smoothing, and use of local representation learner affect reported few-shot performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Self-augmentation raises few-shot accuracy over baseline on miniImageNet and tieredImageNet; LRL adds small 1-shot improvements and larger 5-shot improvements.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Combining self-mix image augmentation with self-distillation improves transfer to unseen classes, with additional gains from task-specific representation learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 5 reports that label smoothing improves baseline base-class accuracy from 80.22% to 81.36% while reducing unseen-class accuracy across the tested methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label smoothing can benefit classification of trained classes while impairing few-shot transfer to unseen classes.

record.problems: The experiments evaluate few-shot classification on classes disjoint from the base training classes, so they do not establish same-distribution train-test gap claims. The principal ablation comparisons are limited to three datasets and two shot settings.
record.rows_left_out: Table 4 includes additional regional-dropout and distillation combinations for miniImageNet, tieredImageNet, and miniImageNet → CUB; these are omitted to keep the extraction focused on baseline, proposed method, and LRL comparisons. Table 2 and Table 3 also report comparisons with prior methods, but those are few-shot results outside the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe, including chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Effects of network dropout, dropout strength, training-set size, or removing dropout and weight decay together.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with train–test gaps, and comparison with norm or margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All twelve extracted values and their stated numeric baselines match Table 4. Their original observed/partial states describe method gains rather than effects named by V1–V8. The exclusion rests on the interventions and measurements, not solely on the disjoint-class evaluation setting.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label test performance on held-out examples from the same distribution.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and same-distribution test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparison on same-distribution held-out images.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparisons on same-distribution held-out benchmarks.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects on same-distribution test error in the stated classifier regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements and their relation to same-distribution train-test gaps.
Removal of memorized training examples and resulting same-distribution test accuracy.
